precepts.text: The wicked boasts of his heart's desire and blesses the covetous, whom the Most High abhors, and will not seek after God.
precepts.point: The transgression of the wicked says there is no fear of God before his eyes, for he flatters himself in his own eyes. He boasts himself up: nobody could take me down.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“The transgression of the wicked saith within my heart, that there is no fear of God before his eyes. For he flattereth himself in his own eyes”. He boasts himself up: nobody could take me down. Psalm 10 shows the same wicked one: “For the wicked boasteth of his heart’s desire, and blesseth the covetous, whom the Lord abhorreth.” He boasts, he blesses the covetous whom the Most High abhors, and he will not seek after God; there is no fear of God before his eyes.

“The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit: he hath left off to be wise, and to do good.” The wickedness of this nation gets worse and worse. People who have changed what the Most High made them are now over the educational system, showing children sexual things they are not even supposed to know exist. Yet those same children they say are not fit to choose which parent they want to be with; they put up laws and red tape to keep a child from the parent they want to be around.

precepts.text: Edom is the border of wickedness, the beginning and ending of all wickedness; a border is where something starts and where it ends, and that border of wickedness is Esau, who is the wicked one doing all this boasting.
precepts.point: The transgression of the wicked says there is no fear of God before his eyes, for he flatters himself in his own eyes. He boasts himself up: nobody could take me down.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
Who is the wicked one doing all this boasting? “Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith the Lord of hosts, They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.” Edom is the border of wickedness.

A border is where something starts and where it ends. Edom is the beginning and the ending of all wickedness, and that border of wickedness is Esau. He is the one who flatters himself in his own eyes, whose mouth is iniquity and deceit, and who “deviseth mischief upon his bed”. Esau does this all the time; they devise iniquity on their beds, and the Lord has indignation against them for ever.

precepts.text: Woe to them that devise iniquity and work evil upon their beds, and when the morning is light they practice it, because it is in the power of their hand.
precepts.point: The wickedness of this nation gets worse and worse. People who have changed what the Most High made them are now over the educational system, showing children sexual things they are not even supposed to know exist. Yet those same children they say are not fit to choose which parent they want to be with; they put up laws and red tape to keep a child from the parent they want to be around.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“He deviseth mischief upon his bed; he setteth himself in a way that is not good; he abhorreth not evil.” Micah pronounces the judgment on it: “Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.” They plan it at night and carry it out in the morning, because right now the power is in their hand.

While we are sleeping, they are up thinking how to take us down, whether it be our own people or the wicked Esau of the other nations. While we do the work and study the word, they are typing on Facebook figuring out how to take us down. That is why when Christ said we would be hated of all nations, he meant all nations, including our own nation.

precepts.text: After all our evil deeds and great trespass, the Most High punished us less than our iniquity deserved and gave us such deliverance as this; we deserve far worse, but because of his loving kindness he punished us less.
precepts.point: We cannot take anything we do for granted or get high-minded in this truth and think we cannot be touched. Remember this one thing above all.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“Thy mercy, O Lord, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds. Thy righteousness is like the great mountains; thy judgments are a great deep”. Ezra shows what that mercy looks like on Israel: “after all that is come upon us for our evil deeds, and for our great trespass, seeing that thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve, and hast given us such deliverance as this”. We deserve far worse, but because of his lovingkindness he punished us less than our iniquity deserved and gave us such deliverance as this.

That is why we cannot take anything we do for granted, or get high-minded in this truth and think we cannot be touched. What we have is mercy. Remember this one thing above all.

precepts.text: He that is athirst is given of the fountain of the water of life freely, talking about us getting the kingdom and eternal life; he that overcometh shall inherit all things.
precepts.point: Because of his loving kindness, they shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of his house and drink of the river of his pleasures, for with him is the fountain of life and in his light we shall see light.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light.” John sees that fountain given out: “I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely.” This is us getting the kingdom and eternal life; he that overcometh shall inherit all things.

Because of his lovingkindness, “They shall be abundantly satisfied with the fatness of thy house; and thou shalt make them drink of the river of thy pleasures.” If we keep the commandments, we are going to see that kingdom of heaven and the fatness of his house. That is why Paul says to set your affection on things above.

precepts.text: Refrain from these men and let them alone, for if this work be of men it will come to naught, but if it be of God you cannot overthrow it, lest you be found to fight against God.
precepts.point: When we keep the commandments, those who devise wickedness against us are going to get cast down, whether it be another nation or one of our own people. If you come against the work of the Most High, you are fighting against him, not against the man you see with your face.

note.label: Psalm 36: The Transgression of the Wicked

precepts.why:
“Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked remove me. There are the workers of iniquity fallen: they are cast down, and shall not be able to rise.” Acts shows why they fall: “Refrain from these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men, it will come to nought: But if it be of God, ye cannot overthrow it; lest haply ye be found even to fight against God.”

When we keep the commandments, those who devise wickedness against us are going to get cast down, whether it be another nation or one of our own people. If you come against the work of the Most High, you are fighting against him, not against the man you see with your face, and you cannot overthrow it.

When we keep the commandments, like Deacon Yawasap says, the angels get activated, and when the angels get activated our enemies get the destruction coming to them, no matter how much they have.
